newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dlr recovery threatened by Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dlr recovery threatened by Tokyo.

text.p: The Australian dollar came under renewed pressure late Friday, but kept a grip on a key trendline offering the chance of an end to its 2-month downtrend.
The currency had reached as high as US$0.7730 offshore after upbeat jobs data soothed fears of another rate cut and prompted heavy short covering along with new U.S. and Swiss buying.

It was slapped back by sales from a New York bank, however, and surrendered more ground today as a Japanese securities house sold into strength. The sales from Tokyo disappointed bulls who had thought this source of offers had dried up, but the close above US$0.7625 was enough to keep alive hopes of a bottom.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the local dollar had backtracked to US$0.7641/46 from an early US$0.7664/69 and Thursday's firm US$0.7675/80 finish.
That was still well above the week's US$0.7550 low and, crucially, above former trendline resistance at US$0.7625.

This had guided the currency down since early December when it topped out at a six year high of US$0.8212 and analysts thought a weekly finish above there would be a big step toward ending the downtrend. Confirmation would require clearing resistance at US$0.7735 and most reckoned a period of consolidation was needed before that could be accomplished.

But traders cautioned if the currency cracked that trendline it would indicate Thursday's 1-/12 cent jump had been a false recovery and a renewed test of US$0.7550 support was on the way. On the crosses the currency was holding firm close to 4-1/2 year highs on the yen at 95.30/40 unchanged from Wednesday, and near a five year peak on the mark at 1.2890/04 from 1.2986/10.

The dollar had cleared a long term resistance level against the mark which stretched back to November 1991 and had capped major rallies in 1992 and 1994. The break of such a long standing barrier was considered very bullish and opened the way for an extended uptrend to the 1991 peak around 1.4250 marks.

Traders cautioned Japanese securities house still had an inclination to sell dollars -- the supply was coming from retail investors redeeming yen/A$ samurais early -- and the dollar above 95.00 would also make it very profitable for them.
The lessened risk of a domestic rate cut had improved the A$'s yield differential, but perhaps not enough to tempt Tokyo.

One reason was Japanese securities houses wanted to diversify their currency risk, which was predominately A$ last year, and that meant issuing all new dual currency samurai bonds largely in U.S. dollars and sterling.

The fundamental support for the dollar may become a little more solid next week if, as expected, the RBA uses its monthly bulletin to reiterate its desire to wait and gauge the impact of the last three easings.
The bulletin includes the bank's quarterly assessment of the economy which Governor Ian Macfarlane this week hinted would take an upbeat view of growth prospects.
